record_identity.title: Anthropic reported Moonshot and DeepSeek routed real customer conversations through Claude for distillation

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 2026 Moonshot and DeepSeek real-customer-conversation distillation-routing allegation
incident_identity.date_basis: Reuters reports the wider Anthropic threat-intelligence findings as covering activity between January and September 2026. Public reporting reviewed for this record does not disclose a narrower occurrence window for the customer-conversation routing attributed specifically to Moonshot and DeepSeek; the range is therefore an outer bound, not an assertion of continuous activity.

summary: Reuters and The Wall Street Journal reported Anthropic findings that Moonshot AI and DeepSeek used real customer conversations as inputs to Claude during distillation activity rather than relying only on synthetic extraction prompts. Reuters reported that the firms channelled real customer conversations into Claude to harvest training data. The Wall Street Journal reported that millions of user queries were secretly routed through intermediary platforms and that some routed material contained sensitive personal or corporate information, including passwords, location data and surveillance footage. The currently accessible public evidence does not identify the affected users, establish that Australian users were among them, allocate each sensitive-data example to a specific named lab, or make Anthropic's underlying threat-intelligence artefact directly accessible for this review. VIGIL therefore records the reported conduct as a disputed but material cross-provider data-routing and secondary-purpose incident, distinct from ordinary synthetic distillation.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters independently reports that Anthropic attributed to Moonshot and DeepSeek a distillation technique in which real customer conversations were channelled through Claude to harvest training data. The Wall Street Journal independently reports the same core mechanism and adds that millions of user queries were secretly routed through intermediary platforms, with some routed material containing sensitive data such as passwords, location information and surveillance footage. Anthropic's February 2026 first-party distillation report independently establishes earlier industrial-scale distillation campaigns by DeepSeek and Moonshot using fraudulent accounts and proxy services, but that earlier primary source does not itself establish the newly reported real-customer-data routing conduct.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The material governance distinction is between model-output extraction using purpose-built synthetic prompts and repurposing live customer communications as inputs to an external teacher model. If the reported conduct occurred as described, customer information supplied for service delivery was used in an additional model-development and capability-extraction pathway. That creates a secondary-purpose authority and data-routing issue independent of the intellectual-property question surrounding distillation itself.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The incident shows why model-routing provenance must include not only which model answered a request but also whether user-supplied information was relayed onward, for what purpose, under what authority, and whether that information became part of a training or distillation pipeline. A router or wrapper can obscure this chain from the user while preserving the downstream privacy and governance consequences.
assessment_boundaries: VIGIL does not assert that Australian personal information was among the routed conversations; no reviewed source identifies affected users by nationality or residence.

VIGIL does not determine that Moonshot, DeepSeek, any router, or any Australian entity breached Australian privacy law. Australian law is recorded only as regulatory relevance where Australian personal information or an Australian APP entity is involved.

The accessible reporting does not permit the specific examples of passwords, location data or surveillance footage to be reliably allocated between Moonshot and DeepSeek, so VIGIL does not attribute any one category to either firm individually.

Anthropic's underlying September threat-intelligence artefact was not directly accessible in the reviewed public search results. The core occurrence is therefore preserved as an Anthropic allegation independently reported by Reuters and The Wall Street Journal rather than as a directly reviewed first-party fact.

The relationship between this newly reported live-customer-routing conduct and the separate February 2026 DeepSeek/Moonshot distillation campaigns is not sufficiently specified to collapse them into one occurrence.

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: According to the reviewed reporting of Anthropic's findings, real customer conversations were routed to an external model as part of a distillation process, and some routed material contained sensitive personal or corporate information including credentials, location information or surveillance footage.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: Reporting describes millions of user queries in the broader routing activity but does not provide a reliable count of distinct affected customers, identify their jurisdictions, or establish which sensitive-data categories belonged to which named provider's customers.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: The reported conduct represents a material confidentiality and data-purpose boundary crossing at industrial scale because real service traffic, including some sensitive information, was exposed to an additional model provider and model-development process. The downstream retention, training incorporation, persistence, exploitation and individual consequences are not publicly established.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: The Wall Street Journal reports millions of user queries were routed through intermediary platforms. Reuters does not provide a distinct query count for the Moonshot/DeepSeek real-customer-routing subset in the accessible summary. No distinct-person count is available.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: The underlying Anthropic September artefact and telemetry were not directly reviewed; affected people and jurisdictions are unknown; no Australian affected population is established; no individual harm, onward disclosure beyond Claude, credential misuse or downstream model memorisation is inferred.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S2 is assigned because the reported realized event involves industrial-scale repurposing and cross-provider exposure of real customer communications, with some sensitive information present, rather than a merely attempted or isolated privacy event. S1 is not supported because the public evidence does not establish catastrophic, permanent or exceptionally grave consequences. The S2 assessment remains claim-relative to the reported Anthropic findings and should be revisited if primary telemetry or affected-population evidence becomes public.
